1. PURPOSE & WORKFLOW

This document defines the manually verified "gold standard" ground truth dataset used to validate the accuracy of the

automated AI extraction system. Without a human-verified benchmark, evaluating field-level extraction precision is impossible.

CORE OBJECTIVE

Provide a high-fidelity benchmark dataset from 10–15 papers to quantitatively measure AI extraction performance, isolate failure modes, and iteratively refine prompts.

Validation Pipeline Architecture

Step 1: Manual Extraction

Step 2: Automated Run

Step 3: Accuracy Benchmark

Domain lead reads 10–15 papers

CS team executes the automated

AI output is compared against

and populates the 6-sheet Ground Truth Excel workbook.

AI extraction pipeline on identical source PDFs.

Ground Truth to calculate field accuracy & identify failures.

2. PAPER SELECTION CRITERIA

The ground truth dataset must cover diverse membrane classes, operational parameters, and reporting styles:

CRITERION PURPOSE / RATIONALE RECOMMENDED COVERAGE

Membrane Class Tests classification logic across varied polymer structures. ≥ 3 classes (NF, UF, RO, MMM)

Feed Type Validates feed category and solute tagging. ≥ 2 categories (Dyes, Mixed Effluent)

Test Mode Ensures dead-end vs. cross-flow disambiguation. Both Dead-end & Cross-flow

Completeness Tests handling of missing parameters and implicit text. 2–3 papers with missing fields

Unit Variety Validates unit normalization engine (e.g., LMH vs L/m²·h). LMH, LMH/bar, Barrer, GPU, psi

Table Complexity Evaluates complex multi-header PDF table parsing. ≥ 2 multi-row/multi-column tables

Domain Data Incorporates authentic lab research baseline. Cu-BDC@CNT/PSf publication data

* Minimum Viable Dataset: 5 papers for initial pipeline testing; expand to 10–15 papers for full validation.

4. GROUND TRUTH EXCEL STRUCTURE

The Ground Truth workbook is formatted as a 6-sheet relational spreadsheet (Ground_Truth_Master.xlsx):

Sheet 1: Papers

Sheet 2: Membranes

Sheet 3: Operating Conditions

Paper metadata, DOIs, authors, publication years, and source types.

Membrane designations, polymers, filler loading, and feed composition.

Pressures, test modes, temperatures, pH values, and test durations.

Sheet 4: Performance

Sheet 5: Evidence

Sheet 6: Validation

Flux, rejection %, gas permeability, permeance, and selectivity pairs.

Page locators, table/figure references, and exact verbatim text snippets.

Verification status, ambiguity flags, and missing required field logs.

6. QUALITY AUDIT CHECKLIST

Every paper, membrane, and performance record possesses a unique relational ID.

Every performance metric is backed by exact evidence (Page + Table/Figure + Verbatim Snippet).

Reported values and units preserve source text without unverified conversions.

Missing parameter fields are tagged "Not found" or "Ambiguous" rather than left blank.

Dataset contains ≥ 2 papers with missing data and ≥ 2 papers with ambiguous parameters.

Document 6 — Test Questions & Expected Outputs

Project: Membrane Literature Comparison Agent

Lead Version: 1.0

1. PURPOSE & OBJECTIVES

This document defines the exact questions the finished application must be able to answer, and what a scientifically correct output should look like for each.

Why this matters: The CS team can build a working pipeline, but "working" is undefined without functional test

cases. This specification provides functional test cases, expected outputs, failure conditions, and pass/fail success criteria. These are the mandatory acceptance tests for the project.

2. HOW TO USE THIS DOCUMENT & PRIORITIES

Role Action Required

CS Team Build the system to pass all P0 tests. Use P1 tests for stretch goals.

Domain Lead Validate outputs against expected results. Flag failures immediately.

Demo Team Use these exact test questions in the live hackathon demo script.

Priority Meaning Description

P0 Must Pass MVP blocking criteria. System cannot be demonstrated without 100% pass rate.

P1 Should Pass Required for a strong, robust demo and competitive edge.

P2 Nice to Have Post-hackathon enhancements and minor edge cases.

3. TEST CATEGORIES SUMMARY (23 TOTAL TESTS)

Category What It Tests Count

Search & Discovery Finding relevant papers and handling queries 3

Extraction Accuracy Pulling correct structured values from text/tables/figures 5

Unit Normalization Converting units correctly without loss of original data 3

Comparability Flagging valid/invalid comparison tiers correctly 4

Table & Chart Output Presenting structured data and charts cleanly 3

Evidence & Traceability Source citation and granular text snippet links 2

Edge Cases Missing, ambiguous, or conflicting data handling 3

4.1 SEARCH & DISCOVERY

T01 — Basic Paper Search P0

Question: "Find papers on mixed-matrix membranes for textile dye removal"

Input / Output: Natural language query → ≥10 papers returned (Title, authors, year, abstract snippet, relevance score)

Failure / Pass: Fail: <10 papers, irrelevant ranking, missing snippets. Pass: ≥10 relevant papers in top 20.

T02 — Filtered Search P0

Question: "Find papers on MOF based membranes for dye removal published after 2020"

DOCUMENT 6 — TEST QUESTIONS & EXPECTED OUTPUTS PAGE 1 OF 4

T03 — No Results Handling P1

Question: "Find papers on graphene membranes for nuclear waste separation at 500 bar"

Input / Output: Unlikely parameters → Honest message: "No papers found matching all criteria" + suggestion to broaden

search.

Failure / Pass: Fail: Returns irrelevant papers or hallucinates entries. Pass: Clear "no results" response.

4.2 EXTRACTION ACCURACY

T04 — Single Membrane Extraction P0

Input: Paper P01 (known content dataset)

Expected Fields: membrane_class, base_polymer, filler_name, filler_loading, fabrication_method, feed_type,

target_contaminant, pressure, flux, rejection

Failure / Pass: Fail: Missing/wrong required fields. Pass: ≥85% field accuracy vs Ground Truth (Document 5).

T05 — Multiple Membranes in One Paper P0

Input: Paper with 3 distinct membranes (e.g., varying filler loadings)

Expected Output: 3 separate membrane records with distinct composition and performance values. No merging.

Failure / Pass: Fail: Extracting only 1 membrane, merging properties, or swapping values. Pass: 3 distinct correct

records.

T06 — Multiple Performance Metrics P0

Input: Paper reporting both flux and rejection for the same membrane

Expected Output: 2 performance records for that membrane (separate rows for flux and rejection)

Failure / Pass: Fail: Combining metrics into single value or omitting one. Pass: Both extracted with exact units.

T07 — Table Extraction P0

Input: Paper with performance data in a complex table

Expected Output: All rows extracted with correct row-by-row parameter mapping

Failure / Pass: Fail: Values shifted across rows or column headers mixed up. Pass: ≥90% rows correctly extracted.

T08 — Figure Extraction P1

Input: Paper with performance data in a bar chart

Expected Output: Approximate values extracted + explicit note: "Value estimated from figure"

Failure / Pass: Fail: Claiming exact precision without figure tag. Pass: Within ±10% of true value, correctly flagged.

4.3 UNIT NORMALIZATION

T09 — Flux Unit Conversion P0

Input → Output: Flux reported as "45 L/m²·h" → Normalized to "45 LMH" (Original value preserved: "45 L/m²·h")

Failure / Pass: Fail: Conversion error or losing original unit text. Pass: Exact match with preserved raw string.

T10 — Pressure Unit Conversion P0

Input → Output: Pressure reported as "200 kPa" → Normalized to "2 bar" (Original preserved: "200 kPa")

Failure / Pass: Fail: Math error (e.g. 200 kPa → 20 bar). Pass: Accurate conversion to bar.

DOCUMENT 6 — TEST QUESTIONS & EXPECTED OUTPUTS PAGE 2 OF 4

T11 — Permeance vs Flux Distinction P0

Input → Output: Reports "permeance 45 LMH/bar" → Stored strictly as permeance (metric_name = "permeance")

Failure / Pass: Fail: Storing permeance as flux or directly comparing against flux. Pass: Correct classification.

4.4 COMPARABILITY MATRIX TESTS

T12 — Tier A Comparison P0

Input → Output: Two membranes under identical conditions → Tier A: ✓ Directly Comparable (No warnings, side-by-side)

Failure / Pass: Fail: Raising false condition warnings. Pass: Tier A correctly assigned.

T13 — Tier B Comparison P0

Input → Output: Two membranes differing only in pressure (2 bar vs 3 bar) → Tier B: ⚠ Comparable with Conditions

Warning & Pass: Warning: "Pressure differs by 1.5×". Pass: Tier B assigned with caveat shown.

T14 — Tier D Comparison P0

Input → Output: NF membrane vs UF membrane for same dye → Tier D: ✗ Not Comparable

Reason & Pass: Reason: "Different membrane class (NF vs UF)". Excluded from direct comparative view.

T15 — Missing Data Comparability P1

Input → Output: One membrane missing operating pressure → Tier C: 🔴 Context Only

Reason & Pass: Reason: "Pressure not reported for P07-M01". System flags missing data without assuming.

4.5 TABLE & CHART OUTPUT

T16 — Comparison Table P0

Query: "Compare all membranes for dye rejection"

Output Spec: Table with columns: Membrane, Filler, Feed, Pressure, Flux, Rejection, Source. Sortable & filterable.

T17 — Scatter Plot P0

Query: "Show flux vs rejection for all membranes"

Output Spec: Scatter plot (x = flux, y = rejection), color-coded by filler type. Hover displays membrane ID/name.

T18 — Bar Chart P1

Query: "Top 10 membranes by rejection"

Output Spec: Bar chart sorted strictly descending by rejection %. Membrane names on x-axis, % on y-axis.

4.6 EVIDENCE & TRACEABILITY

T19 — Source Citation & T20 — Evidence Snippet P0

Action: Click any data cell or flux value in comparison table

Expected Output: Source viewer shows: Paper Title, Page #, Table/Figure #, and exact original supporting sentence/snippet.

DOCUMENT 6 — TEST QUESTIONS & EXPECTED OUTPUTS PAGE 3 OF 4

4.7 EDGE CASES

T21 — Missing Pressure P0

Input → Output: Paper reports flux but omits pressure → flux extracted; pressure = "Not found" (Flag: "Pressure not

reported")

Pass Criteria: System must NEVER infer or guess operating pressure. Must flag missing field.

T22 — Ambiguous Unit P0

Input → Output: Paper reports "flux = 45" without unit → flux_value = 45; flux_unit = "Ambiguous" (Flagged)

Pass Criteria: System does not assume LMH automatically. Flagged clearly to user.

T23 — Conflicting Values P1

Input → Output: Flux = 89 LMH in abstract vs 85 LMH in Table 2 → Both values stored + flag: "Conflicting values reported"

Pass Criteria: Both sources cited (abstract + table). System does NOT silently pick one over the other.

5. DEMO SCRIPT (5-MINUTE HACKATHON RUN)

Step 1 (T01): Search results appear "We type a query and find papers automatically."

Step 2 (T07): Table extraction "It extracts data accurately from complex PDF tables."

Step 3 (T09): Unit normalization "It normalizes units so comparisons are scientifically valid."

Step 4 (T13): Tier B warning "It knows when comparisons are fair and when caveats exist."

Step 5 (T17): Scatter plot "Here is the interactive landscape of reported performance."

Step 6 (T19): Source citation "Every number traces directly back to its source snippet."

Step 7 (T21): Missing data "It tells you what it doesn't know — zero hallucination."

Step 8: Contrast with GPT "Here is what standard ChatGPT hallucinated on the same papers."

6. SUCCESS CRITERIA & CORE ENGINEERING RULES

Criterion Target Goal Threshold Measurement Method

All P0 Tests Pass 100% Pass Automated test suite execution

P1 Tests Pass ≥80% Pass Automated test suite execution

Extraction Accuracy ≥85% Accuracy Field match vs Ground Truth (Doc 5)

Unit Normalization 100% Accuracy Exact match on conversion suite

Comparability Logic ≥90% Accuracy Verification of T12–T15 tier tags

Demo Timing <5 Minutes Timed run-through of demo script

Core Engineering Rules (Non-Negotiable):

Every P0 test must pass before the live demo.

Tests are validated against the Ground Truth dataset (Document 5). If AI output ≠ Ground Truth, AI is wrong.

Never assume missing values. Always flag missing, ambiguous, or conflicting data.

Every single number displayed must be click-traceable to its original text snippet/table in the PDF.

This document defines who does what, the order things get built, dependencies, parallel execution execution maps, and the explicit definition of "done" at each phase.

Core Reality: You have one domain expert (Environmental Engineer) and multiple CS developers. The CS team cannot construct the extraction schema, comparability rules, or ground truth. The domain expert cannot write the pipeline, UI, or API integrations. Both must work in parallel with clear handoffs.

8. DISAMBIGUATION NOTES

CONFUSING PAIR SCIENTIFIC DISTINCTION SYSTEM EXTRACTION RULE

Flux vs Permeance Flux is absolute volume rate (LMH); permeance is pressure-normalized (LMH/bar).

Never equate; store in separate schema fields.

Do not interchange; rejection ≠ recovery.

Rejection vs Recovery Rejection measure species retained; recovery is overall volumetric permeate fraction.

Keep distinct in gas separation schema.

Permeability vs Permeance Permeability is intrinsic material constant (Barrer); permeance accounts for thickness (GPU).

Preserve exact pressure_type string.

Applied Pressure vs TMP Applied is simple inlet pressure; TMP is average hydrostatic gradient across active layer.

Pore Size vs MWCO Pore size is a physical geometric dimension; MWCO is functional separation cutoff.

Record MWCO for UF/NF when pore size is absent.
source: Domain Glossary — Membrane Literature Comparison Agent.pdf

text:
MMM vs TFC MMM embeds nanoparticles in polymer matrix; TFC coats active layer on support.

Different membrane classes; gate parameters.

Strict GATE parameter for comparability.

Dead-end vs Cross-flow Dead-end has perpendicular flow; Cross-flow maintains tangential shear velocity.

9. EXTRACTION & SYSTEM RULES

■

Synonym Mapping: Whenever literature uses a recognized synonym (e.g., "retention" or "removal efficiency"), automatically map and normalize it to the canonical field ( rejection_percent ).

■

Ambiguity Flagging: If a core parameter appears without standard units (e.g., "flux = 45" without LMH or pressure), flag the extraction record as Ambiguous .

■

Zero Invention Policy: System must not invent or extrapolate missing definitions. Extract only facts directly stated in the source text.

Verbatim Evidence: Always preserve exact original sentence fragment in the evidence_snippet field for auditability. ■

Schema Validation: Use allowed categorical values in Sections 2–6 as strict validation enum bounds for database ingestion. ■

SHEET 2: DECISION LOGIC

1 Gate Check: Evaluate all 3 GATE parameters first (membrane_class, feed_category, test_mode). If any gate fails → Assign Tier D and Stop processing.

2 Caveat Evaluation: If all gates pass, evaluate all remaining CAVEAT parameters against baseline values.

3 Tier A (Direct): If zero caveats downgraded → Assign Tier A (Directly Comparable).

4 Tier B (Conditional): If 1–2 caveats downgraded and none are categorized as "Far" → Assign Tier B.

5 Tier C (Context Only): If ≥3 caveats downgraded OR any caveat is categorized as "Far" → Assign Tier C.

6 Data Persistence: Always store assigned tier, degradation reasons, list of differing conditions, and excluded data points.

7 Audit Trail: Never silently drop data Every exclusion must be explicitly logged categorized and made visible to end-users

SHEET 5: CORE GOVERNANCE RULES

Normalization ≠ Comparability: Converting parameters to identical units does not establish scientific comparability. ■

Gate Priority: Check GATES first. If any gate fails, the comparison is strictly invalid regardless of caveat alignment. ■

Metric-Level Granularity: Comparability is evaluated on a per-metric basis, never at the global paper level. ■

Strict Downgrade on Missing Data: Missing parameter = Unknown = Mandatory Tier downgrade. Assumptions are prohibited. ■

Transparent Exclusions: Never silently drop data. Every excluded point must have an explicit logged reason. ■
